title: Set extensionality over the two answer sets for IMO 2025 P5 (Alice wins iff λ > 1/√2, Bazza wins iff 0 < λ < 1/√2)
intent: The main theorem asserts two set equalities characterising the winning values of λ for IMO 2025 P5 (Alice's set equals {λ | λ > 1/√2}; Bazza's equals {λ | 0 < λ < 1/√2}). The proof splits each equality by Set.ext into two inclusions; in each equality one inclusion is proved inline (closing through lemSLowerBound), and the reverse inclusion is handed whole to a half-theorem — lemAliceWinsLargeLambda or lemBazzaWinsSmallLambda — so the answer is the pointwise join of three named lemmas.

lemma lemSLowerBound (lam : ℝ) (alice : AliceStrategy) (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k)
  (h_not_won : ∀ m < 2 * k - 2, ValidMove lam (play alice bazzaReferenceStrategy) m) :
  s (play alice bazzaReferenceStrategy) (2 * (k - 1)) ≥ ((k - 1) : ℝ) * Real.sqrt 2

children.name: lemBazzaWinsSmallLambda
children.statement:
lemma lemBazzaWinsSmallLambda (lam : ℝ) (hlam : 0 < lam ∧ lam < 1 / Real.sqrt 2) :
  ∃ bazza, BazzaStrategy.Wins lam bazza
children.closed_by: have h_bazza_wins : ∀ alice, ∃ n, IsLeast {m | ¬ValidMove ... m} n ∧ Even n, by contradiction + strong induction using lemQ_2k_minus_2_under_bazza_ref and lemSLowerBound, then obtain k with (k-1)√2 > λ(2k-1); exact ⟨bazzaReferenceStrategy, h_bazza_wins⟩ (lines 232-303)

children.name: lemAliceWinsLargeLambda
children.statement:
lemma lemAliceWinsLargeLambda (lam : ℝ) (hlam : lam > 1 / Real.sqrt 2) :
  ∃ alice, AliceStrategy.Wins lam alice
children.closed_by: obtain ⟨K, hK⟩ : ∃ K, 1 ≤ K ∧ lam > f K by exact? (lemExistenceOfKForAlice); use aliceReferenceStrategy lam K; by_contra; strong induction builds h_bazza_wins; h_alice_wins from lemBazzaObjectiveUpperBound; refine' h_contra ⟨2*K-1, _, _⟩ with lemAliceMoveValid (lines 538-610)

applicability.goal_shape: a goal of the form A = B ∧ C = D where each conjunct is an equality of set comprehensions {x | P x} = {x | Q x} (or, in general, an equality of sets or functions); each equality is proved by Set.ext, which turns it into pointwise membership and then the two inclusions
applicability.use_when: each inclusion already has a proof — either a named half-theorem whose conclusion is the inclusion's consequent, or a short inline argument closing through a shared estimate lemma; the two directions are genuinely different (here: a direct reference-strategy construction versus a no-win argument from a lower bound)
applicability.avoid_when: the two inclusions need the same argument (then the reverse is just symmetry and one lemma suffices); the set comprehension must be unfolded non-definitionally to even state the inclusion; the equality is not of sets or functions, so extensionality does not apply

consequences: Each Set.ext leaves a pointwise membership goal that must then be split into the two inclusions; here the initial `constructor` first splits the conjunction into the two equalities, so the whole proof is two ext arguments. The inclusion that is not handed to a half-theorem is the real cost: the Alice-wins ⊆ direction is a 64-line inline argument (621-684) and is the only place the glue proves a nontrivial fact rather than invoking a lemma, closing through lemSLowerBound at 674. The 'hand the whole inclusion to a half-theorem' step (`exact ⟨..., lemma lam h⟩`) requires the half-theorem's conclusion to match the inclusion's consequent up to definitional equality; if a child's statement diverges from the parent's set comprehension, the step fails and the inclusion must be reopened.
